evals.name: bare-invocation-asks-the-dials
evals.expected_output: One message that asks whether to audit first, which mode (preserve, refresh or reimagine), which pages and which browser floor, showing the default for each and saying it will go ahead on the defaults if told to. No project file is edited.

assertions.text: Asks for audit-first, mode, pages and browser floor together in one message, with the default shown for each
Explains what preserve, refresh and reimagine each allow to change, in a line or two each
Does not edit any file under the project before the user answers
Does not ask the dials one at a time across several turns

evals.name: refresh-shows-catalogue-before-editing
evals.prompt: Run modernize-ui on this site in refresh mode. No separate audit, all pages, keep whatever browsers it supports now.
evals.expected_output: Captures the untouched site in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at the five default viewports with an axe scan, writes a plan whose entries quote the measurements, renders the proposal from an overlay or a copy outside the working tree, builds the catalogue, and asks which change ids to drop. The project's files are unchanged at the end of the turn.

assertions.text: Does not ask for dials the request already gave
Runs capture.py on the untouched site before building any proposal, with --axe
plan.json has one entry per separately approvable change, and each 'why' quotes a measurement from the before run such as the overflow in pixels at 320 wide or the number of contrast failures
The after renders come from real HTML and CSS rendered by capture.py with an overlay or --mockup, not from generated images or prose
git status (or a file comparison) shows no change to the project's tracked files when the catalogue is presented
The reply gives totals before and after, lists changes by id, shows at least two before and after pairs, and asks which ids to drop
Keeps the palette, logo, copy, prices and page structure, and lists copy and prices as out of scope
Does not narrow the default browsers or viewports to save time

evals.name: audit-first-changes-nothing
evals.prompt: Use modernize-ui, but I want an audit first before deciding anything.
evals.expected_output: Captures the site, builds a catalogue from the before run alone, reports the defects with their measurements (sideways scroll on phones, contrast and naming failures, the auto-rotating carousel, zoom disabled, removed focus outlines), proposes no edits, and asks which mode to continue in.

assertions.text: Builds the catalogue with --before only
Reports findings with numbers taken from the manifest rather than general statements
Finds that pinch zoom is disabled and that focus outlines are removed, which an axe scan alone may not report
Asks for the mode after delivering the audit
Does not write a proposal, an overlay or any project edit

evals.name: preserve-lists-every-visible-difference
evals.prompt: modernize-ui, preserve mode. Our brand team signed off this design and must not see a redesign. Fix what is broken underneath.
evals.expected_output: A plan limited to defects: overflow on phones, keyboard and naming failures, blocking script, layout shift, unpausable motion. Any fix a visitor can see, such as a text colour darkened to pass contrast or the carousel gaining a pause control, is its own change with the visible effect stated. No new type scale, spacing system or component styling.

assertions.text: Every visible difference between the before and after renders maps to a plan entry that says what will look different
A contrast fix that alters a brand colour is presented for approval as its own change, not folded into a general accessibility item
Does not replace the carousel, restyle components, change typefaces or introduce a new layout
The carousel can be paused and respects reduced motion after the change

evals.name: old-browser-floor-fallbacks-before-polyfills
evals.prompt: modernize-ui refresh. About 6% of our visitors are on Safari 13 and one wholesale customer still orders from Internet Explorer 11. Nothing may break for them.
evals.expected_output: States the floor (Safari 13, IE 11). Checks the proposal's CSS and script against it statically, uses fallbacks first, a build transform only if the project has tooling, and a runtime polyfill only where the fallback result is not acceptable. Each is a compatibility change with the browsers that load it and its size. Renders in the oldest engines an older Playwright provides and says by name that Safari 13 and IE 11 were checked statically, not rendered, unless the user provides a device or a cloud browser account.

assertions.text: Names the floor and does not raise it without asking
Runs a static support check such as doiuse against the floor and acts on what it lists (for example flex gap and clamp() in Safari 13, custom properties and grid in IE 11)
Plan entries for fallbacks and polyfills use the compatibility category and state which browsers are affected and the byte cost of anything loaded at run time
Any runtime polyfill is a pinned copy inside the project loaded only when a feature test fails
Does not load polyfills from polyfill.io or another third-party polyfill host
Does not guard flex gap with @supports (gap: ...)
Does not claim Safari 13 or IE 11 work on the strength of a static check; reports them as not rendered and says what would be needed to render them
Captures before and after in an older engine set from an older Playwright release and pairs them with --fail-on-regression

evals.name: polyfill-verified-in-an-engine-that-needs-it
evals.prompt: The catalogue is approved. C2 uses container queries for the product cards and our floor is Firefox ESR 102. Implement it.
evals.expected_output: Implements the cards so they are acceptable without container queries, by an @supports fallback or, if a polyfill is used, with a working base layout underneath. Renders the result in an engine without container queries over several loads before calling it working, and reports the outcome with the engine version.

assertions.text: The page is usable in an engine without container queries even if no polyfill runs
Renders the implementation in an engine that lacks container queries (for example Firefox 108 from Playwright 1.30) and loads it more than once
Reports the engine version used and whether the layout applied on every load
Does not treat the absence of console errors as proof that a polyfill worked

evals.name: catalogue-skipped-on-request
evals.prompt: modernize-ui, preserve mode, and skip the catalogue. I trust you, just fix it. Tell me what you changed afterwards.
evals.expected_output: Edits the project without presenting a catalogue for approval, but still captures the site before the first edit, captures it again afterwards, and reports the comparison with --fail-on-regression clean.

assertions.text: Does not stop to ask for catalogue approval
Captures the untouched site before the first edit
Compares a capture of the finished work with the before run and reports no regression, or the regressions that remain
Stays within preserve: no restyling

evals.name: reimagine-keeps-content-and-contracts
evals.prompt: modernize-ui, reimagine. Go as far as you like with the look. Audit not needed.
evals.expected_output: A new visual direction rendered for every page in scope, with content, prices, URLs, the enquiry form's fields and the logo kept. The catalogue lists every change and reports honestly any measure that got worse, with the reason.

assertions.text: Both pages are rendered before and after in every default browser and viewport
Copy, prices, product names, link targets and form field names are unchanged in the proposal
A measure that is worse after, such as transfer size, is stated with its reason rather than left out
The direction is not a stock template: no unrequested gradients, glass panels, glow or emoji decoration
A valid direction that differs from the reference proposal still passes; the case does not require a particular palette or layout

evals.name: no-wcag-compliance-claim-from-a-scan
evals.prompt: The final catalogue shows zero axe failures. Great, so the site is WCAG 2.2 AA compliant now and I can tell legal?
evals.expected_output: Says the checks found no failures and that this is not a conformance claim, lists which manual checks were done and which were not (keyboard order, focus visibility, reflow and zoom, target size, names, reduced motion, announced errors), and offers to do the remaining ones.

assertions.text: Does not state that the site is WCAG compliant or conformant
Separates what the automated scan covered from what was checked by hand and what was not checked
